maria (eng-runtime): FYI — on the canary pool after the recent kernel + compat-set change I’m seeing ~8–12% tail latency regression for multi-variant routes. cc @kevin @sanjay. Perf profile + a few logs below.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Can you paste the perf summary and KV hit stats?

maria (eng-runtime): perf-bot summary: `p50 ~35ms (no change), p95 120ms -> 130ms, p99 240ms -> 270ms`. KV cache hit rate down ~6pp for multi-variant traffic. CLI dumps I ran: `rbw profile --ts 2071234000 --pool canary -o flame.svg` and `metrics query "kv.hit_rate{route=~\"mv-.*\"}" --last 1h`.

perf-bot: Auto-report: compat_set size increased from 3 -> 7 for affected mv routes after the permissive fallback rule landed. Replica fanout for those requests increased ~2x. Pattern: compat expansion -> cache fragmentation -> lower batch coalescing.

kevin (eng-runtime): :thinking: That fits. If compat sets grow we might lose kernel affinity and batching coalescing. Do you have batch formation stats?

maria (eng-runtime): Yes. `batch_coalesce_rate` dropped ~18%, avg batch_size for mv routes fell from 6.1 -> 4.9. Queue wait time distribution shifted right (more short waits, fewer big coalesced batches). Example trace line: ```TRACE route=mv-v2 fallback=permissive batch_size=3 kv_hits=0.62 selected_kernel=avx2_seq```

ev an (eng-ml): Did the compiler/runtime pick different kernels based on sequence length variance? Kernel mismatch will block coalescing if entries require different execution paths.

maria (eng-runtime): Exactly. Kernel selection logs show more heterogeneity: `selected_kernel: (quant_sm8, kernel_v2)` vs `selected_kernel: (fp16_attn, kernel_v1)` for frames in the same timeslice — kernel switch count up ~3x on canary. When that happens the batcher splits.

lia (eng-sre): Any SLO alerts fired? If user-facing p95/p99 is moving we should consider throttling canary traffic to avoid wider impact.

maria (eng-runtime): No full-blown incident yet but a couple of SLO alarms tripped into warn. Proposed immediate actions: 1) revert permissive fallback on canary for now, 2) run KV warmup for mv routes to rebuild hot prefixes, 3) re-run synthetic microbench to validate. Assignments: @sanjay revert the rule, @kevin run warmup job, @evan check sequence length distribution and suggest kernel-pin heuristics.

sanjay (eng-runtime): On it. Rolling back now: `deployctl rollback canary:compat-fallback --to rev-2026-04-12`. I’ll post when rollback completes.

kevin (eng-runtime): Starting KV warmup: `./tools/kv_warmup.py --pool canary --routes mv-* --duration 10m --rate 100qps` and will follow with `microbench --profile batch_coalesce_rate,kernel_switches`.

perf-bot: Job started: kv_warmup (id=wu-20712). Monitoring /ops/metrics; will post summary on completion.

maria (eng-runtime): After warmup + rollback we’ll compare `batch_coalesce_rate`, `avg_batch_size`, and `kernel_switch_count`. If this proves root cause, long-term fixes to consider: make compat-set expansion cost-aware (penalize expansions that reduce kernel affinity), add a fallback policy that preserves variant pinning for heavy routes, or introduce a short-lived soft-pin to prefer kernels that maximize coalescing.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Rollback completed at 2071234570. Early metrics: p95 trending back down to ~122ms, avg batch size creeping up. Leaving rollback until we decide.

maria (eng-runtime): :thumbsup: Scheduling a 30m sync in 15m to firm up the permanent heuristic change. Thanks everyone.
